mutation_targets.rationale: removing this fact lets Alloy materialise two distinct audit entries recording the same (application, prev->new) transition — i.e., a history rewrite, which the append-only invariant exists to forbid.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj e1, e2: AuditEntry | e1.application = e2.application and e1.prevStatus = e2.prevStatus and e1.newStatus = e2.newStatus and e1.prevStatus = Pending and e1.newStatus = UnderReview }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing the schema-level no-self-assignment lets Alloy assign an application's officer to be the same user as the applicant, which FR-011 and the CHECK constraint forbid.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NoSelfAssignment { some a: LoanApplication | some a.assignedOfficer and a.assignedOfficer = a.applicant }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing this fact lets Alloy invent an application whose current status has no witnessing audit entry — exactly the 'observable state change without audit' case that SC-008 forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenessViolation { some a: LoanApplication | a.status = Approved and no e: AuditEntry | e.application = a and e.newStatus = Approved }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing the enforcement fact while keeping the matrix definition lets Alloy materialise an operation whose caller's role set has no allowed cell for the operation's kind — the canonical least-privilege violation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some op: Operation | op.kind = PatchStatus and OfficerRole not in op.caller.roles and AuditorRole not in op.caller.roles }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing the outcome-binding fact lets Alloy mark an unauthorised GET as OkSuccess — leaking the existence of an application to a caller who is neither the applicant, the assigned officer, nor an auditor.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NoLeakageViolation { some op: Operation | op.kind = GetApplicationOp and op.outcome = OkSuccess and some op.target and op.caller != op.target.applicant and op.caller != op.target.assignedOfficer and AuditorRole not in op.caller.roles }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing the in-flight uniqueness fact lets Alloy create two simultaneous in-flight applications for the same applicant, which the partial-unique index in data-model.md structurally forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OneInFlightViolation { some disj a1, a2: LoanApplication | a1.applicant = a2.applicant and a1.status in (Pending + UnderReview) and a2.status in (Pending + UnderReview) }
